The passage gives Eq. (4): w_i = exp(-β(U_θ(S_i) − U_θ̂(S_i))) divided by the sum over j of the same exponential. The sum runs over the N states of the trajectory, which the passage describes as subsampled and retained, so "retained states" is consistent with Figure 1.

The probabilities p_θ(S_i) ~ exp(-βH(S_i)) are stated, and H is the sum of potential and kinetic energy, with β = 1/(k_B T). All of this is in the passage.

The kinetic energy cancels, as the passage says. The answer's explanation is that it appears identically in the numerator and denominator of the ratio p_θ/p_θ̂. The passage says only "the kinetic energy cancels" and does not say why. The explanation follows directly from the ratio in Eq. (3), though, since the kinetic energy is the same for both potentials.
